title: License to Drill Act
summary: Federal law requires the Bureau of Land Management to charge a fee on every new application to drill for oil and gas on federal land, with the money going into a fund used to speed up permit processing. That fee requirement was set to wind down in 2026. This bill extends it through 2037 and directs that all of the fees collected each year from 2027 through 2037 go into the BLM Permit Processing Improvement Fund.
brief: Extends the BLM oil and gas drilling-permit application fee through 2037 and routes all collected fees into the BLM Permit Processing Improvement Fund.

top_lines.headline: What the Drilling Permit Fee Does
subs: BLM charges a fee on each new application for a permit to drill on federal land
Fees feed the BLM Permit Processing Improvement Fund, used to process permits

top_lines.headline: What This Bill Changes
subs: Extends the fee-collection requirement from 2026 to 2037
Directs all fees collected for fiscal years 2027-2037 to the Improvement Fund

likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Rep. Kennedy (R-UT) with 3 cosponsors in a Republican-majority House, the bill extends an existing energy-permitting fee rather than creating a new program, which limits cost objections. It passed the House by voice vote, but its narrow fee-extension scope leaves Senate scheduling uncertain.

items.main: Names the Act the “License to Drill Act”.
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — BLM Oil and Gas Permit Processing Fee

items.main: Amends Section 35(d) of the Mineral Leasing Act to extend the drilling-permit application fee collection period and redirect the proceeds.
items.detail: Paragraphs (1) and (4) are amended by striking '2026' and inserting '2037', extending the fee requirement by eleven years. Paragraph (3) is rewritten so that, for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2037, all of the fees collected under the subsection are transferred to the BLM Permit Processing Improvement Fund, replacing the prior partial-transfer formula. The bill does not state the dollar amount of the fee.

featured_quotes.name: Ms. Stansbury
featured_quotes.text: This bill would reauthorize a commonsense permitting program, allowing the Bureau of Land Management to continue collecting fees with applications for permits to drill oil and gas wells. These fees go into the Permit Processing Improvement Fund, which funds the expert staff responsible for processing drilling permits, conducting inspections, and ensuring compliance with environmental laws. Studies have consistently found that understaffing at agencies is one of the most common causes of permitting delays.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Kennedy
featured_quotes.text: This bill ensures the Federal Government has the operational resources to process energy permits efficiently without unnecessary delay. Every American takes part in an electrified economy, whether they choose to or not, and right now that economy is facing a critical point. We are heading toward a severe energy deficit. We possess the most dynamic economy in the world, but every single engine of that economy runs on power.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Stauber
featured_quotes.text: Now more than ever, the United States needs to be bringing more energy online to drive our 21st century economy. These bills will help guarantee we have durable, proenergy policy no matter who is in the White House. These pieces of legislation will provide much-needed certainty for domestic energy producers, ensuring leaseholders will be able to responsibly produce on Federal lands, including onshore oil and gas and geothermal energy development.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Westerman
featured_quotes.text: America has some of the richest energy resources in the world, and House Republicans are working alongside the Trump administration to put those resources to work.

gaps: The bill extends and fully redirects the application fee to the BLM Permit Processing Improvement Fund but does not set or adjust the dollar amount of the fee itself.
The bill routes all collected fees into the permit-processing fund through 2037 but does not specify any performance target, such as a permit-processing time the additional funding must achieve.
The bill extends the fee through 2037 but does not address what happens to fee collection after that date.
